title: The Clue in the Shopping Cart
subtitle: A real decision told through the lens of Lynch.
hook: A product you love is a clue, not a conclusion. The filing must still answer the question.
learning_goal: Learn to turn daily observation into a falsifiable hypothesis, then verify it in filings and valuation.

cast.name: Lynch
cast.intro: The story uses Lynch's public record as context, not as an imitation performance.
cast.rule: The narrator explains choices and pressure without changing the historical record.

roles.title: Evidence researcher
roles.pressure: The room wants a fast answer.

narrator.name: Historical decision narrator
narrator.rule: Explain the player's choice, pressure, and learning point without inventing facts.

scenes.title: The Clue in the Shopping Cart
lines: A product is popular in stores and in your own life. That is useful only if it creates a question the filing can test.
Start by writing the hypothesis before buying the story.

actions.label: Build the evidence chain
actions.prompt: Turn the story into variables you can verify.
actions.consequence: You turn observation to hypothesis into a checklist. The next decision must answer what drives the business and what can break it.
actions.narration: A useful story creates a question that can be falsified.

actions.label: Trust the strongest narrative
actions.prompt: The story is popular, simple, and emotionally convincing.
actions.consequence: You gain speed but lose the evidence chain. The next pressure is to explain what your shortcut cannot see.
actions.narration: Confidence is not evidence just because many people share it.

scenes.title: Separate observation from evidence.
lines: Growth must show up in revenue, profit, cash, and a sensible price.

actions.label: Write the failure case first
actions.prompt: Define the evidence that would change your mind.
actions.consequence: You keep growth quality separate from the final price. The decision is now auditable even if the outcome is uncertain.
actions.result_title: The failure case gets a seat
actions.narration: Good decisions preserve the ability to make the next decision.

actions.label: Let the story decide
actions.prompt: The opportunity feels too obvious to delay.
actions.consequence: You turn uncertainty into a position before defining the loss path.
actions.narration: The most dangerous shortcut is the one that feels like courage.

beats.title: The Clue in the Shopping Cart
lines: A product you love is a clue, not a conclusion. The filing must still answer the question.
You are not predicting a price. You are deciding what must be understood before capital is committed.

beats.title: The result is not the lesson

quote.src: Lynch public letters and historical record
quote.text: The public record preserves the decision context, the evidence, and the consequences.
quote.orig: The public record preserves the decision context, the evidence, and the consequences.

lines: History lets you inspect the ending. The skill is learning what could have been known before the ending.

beats.title: What the method adds
beats.them: Learn to turn daily observation into a falsifiable hypothesis, then verify it in filings and valuation.
beats.canon: Use observation to hypothesis, growth quality, and valuation discipline as separate checks.
beats.knowhow: Make the decision explainable before you make it confident.

beats.title: A reusable decision loop
beats.rule: Turn an exciting story into a falsifiable question, then price the uncertainty.
beats.label: observation to hypothesis -> growth quality -> valuation discipline
beats.boundary: No single ratio, headline, or reputation can replace the full chain.
beats.formula: Decision quality = evidence clarity x risk budget x reviewability

beats.title: A new case arrives
beats.question: What is the strongest next move?

options.t: Write a falsifiable claim and a failure case
Use the famous investor as the thesis

beats.fb: A famous investor can give you a method. The evidence still has to be yours.
